One in-house app. Over $80,000 in annual subscriptions removed.

How Ben Young replaced every SaaS app in his business with one in-house app, removing over $80,000 in annual subscriptions and making everyday changes faster.

By Ben Young · Business owner & AI consultant
Updated 16 November 2026

On this page
  • One app built around our business
  • The number — and what it means
  • The part I value most: the speed of improvement
  • What this means for your business
  • Start with a conversation

In my own business, we replaced every SaaS app with one app built in-house. That removed over $80,000 in annual subscriptions and gave us a way to improve the software directly as our team found better ways to work.

One app built around our business

Our business now uses the in-house app in place of the SaaS tools we previously subscribed to. That experience is the foundation of my consulting work: I’ve made this change inside my own business and use the result with my own team.

The number — and what it means

Over $80,000 in annual subscriptions removed. This is the subscription spend cut from my business. It is not a claim that a custom app has no running costs, or that another business will save the same amount.

A fair comparison for your business needs to include development, hosting, AI usage, maintenance and ongoing support. The opportunity depends on your existing software costs and how your team works.

The part I value most: the speed of improvement

“If a team member has an idea of what could be improved in the morning, by lunchtime it’s live.”

That describes what is possible for improvements in our own app. Bigger changes still need scoping, testing and time. The useful shift is being able to act on a team member’s feedback directly.

What this means for your business

Your first step doesn’t have to be a complete replacement. It could be connecting two systems, drafting a report from job notes, or building a small tool for a workflow your current software handles poorly.

I can help assess the practical options and work with you on a defined project. If replacing your platform is on the table, start with the questions to ask before changing job management software.
